clauses.reason: whole: EO 12189 (signed 1980-01-16, 45 FR 3559) amends EO 12153, as amended by EO 12186, to read as a restated section 1-101 to 1-104 exempting first sales of heavy crude oil from price controls under the Emergency Petroleum Allocation Act of 1973, with two definitions of 'heavy crude oil' (one for August 17 through December 20, 1979 and one from December 21, 1979 'and thereafter') and an authority for the Secretary of Energy to adopt regulations. The restated text includes the words "1-103. Effective D ecem ber 21,1 9 7 9  and thereafter," so the clause has no own-terms end; the dated window in the earlier definition ended on December 20, 1979, before the order was signed, and does not end the exemption. First end: EO 12553 (signed 1986-02-25): "it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" followed by a two-column 'No. Subject' table; the entry at offset 26794 of the held EO_12553.txt reads "12189", which matches this order's number and subject. EO 12553 has no effective-date wording, so the revocation is read as effective on signing, 1986-02-25. The Office of the Federal Register catalog note reads "Revoked by: EO 12553, February 25, 1986". The held EO 12553 text prints this part of the table (PDF page 14) as a number-only column followed by a separate subject column: the number 12189 is the 25th entry and pairs with the 25th subject, "Relating to the definition of heavy oil" (offset 28862), consistent with this order's subject. An independent AI-reviewed ACT record for the same pair is carried in the dossier and agrees.
